subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance use this opt-in config plus generic queue callback, or should OpenClaw define a host-owned default timeout and cooperative cancellation contract instead?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound, but source review cannot decide the permanent public configuration and plugin lifecycle contracts or whether an unconfigured upgrade should continue permitting the reported hang.

options.title: Define the canonical cancellation contract
options.body: Keep the fence and persistence work, but establish a host-owned finite timeout and cooperative cancellation or serialization rule before landing the public surface.

options.title: Accept the opt-in contract
options.body: Land the new key and queue callback as permanent APIs while explicitly accepting that the default remains unbounded and timed-out plugin work may continue.

options.title: Pause for plugin API design
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and defer this PR until ContextEngine.maintain() has an owner-approved cancellation contract.

recommendation.title: Define the canonical cancellation contract
recommendation.body: Keep the fence and persistence work, but establish a host-owned finite timeout and cooperative cancellation or serialization rule before landing the public surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties jalehman to the context-engine and runtime transcript-rewrite contracts being changed.
